messages:
sara: quick heads-up — noticed a spike in fncall schema rejections this morning from a customer canary. looks like tool responses containing extra top-level fields are getting hard-failed by the validator. example payload we saw:

sara: ```json
{"status":"ok","result":{"text":"done"},"trace_id":"abc123","_internal_metadata":{"latency_ms":12}}
```

sara: validator error: `unexpected_properties: ['_internal_metadata']` and we return a structured reject to the user which kills the flow.

max: ugh. are we treating unknown props as reject vs ignore right now?

kai: we opted for strict-by-default in the last rollout so tool authors get visible errors. but for fncall we promised a softer migration path. maybe this slipped through the toggle?

liz: @kai can you confirm if the canary used the permissive flag?

kai: checking logs... looks like canary flag was OFF for that tenant.

max: we should not hard-fail on unknown fields for tool responses until partners update. propose: soft-reject (log + telemetry + passthrough) for 2 weeks, then hard after notices.

liz: agreed. also need console surface: show reject_count and last_example per route + sample sanitized payload in the route details. ops keeps getting paged.

max: telemetry addition: `fncall.reject_rate_by_route` + `fncall.reject_examples.sampled` (include truncated payload and validator message). sample size 1 per minute per route should be enough.

kai: implementation note: we need to be careful with PII in sampled payloads — strip fields named `ssn`, `email` etc. add redaction at ingestion.

sara: also noticed billing implications. current hard-reject path refunds tokens for the model but still counts a tool call. product wants consistent billing + clear UX.

max: we can make two changes: 1) route-level toggle `fncall.unknown_props_policy` with enum `strict|permissive|log-only`; 2) console toggle to flip the canary for accounts. default permissive for existing customers, strict for new ones.

liz: docs + changelog needed. and a rollout plan: enable permissive by default for all non-enterprise for 7 days, send partner notices, then move to queued enforcement where customers get 30d to adapt.

kai: for quick patch, I can change validator to soft-fail if `unknown_properties` only, emit a metric `fncall.unknown_prop_softfail` and keep current reject metric for other errors. will open PR.

sara: perfect. @deploy-bot can we gate the soft-fail behind a feature flag so we can roll back if telemetry shows unexpected degens?

deploy-bot: @sara feature flag `fncall:permissive-unknown-props` created (flag-id: ff-7721). default OFF in prod, ON in canary namespaces `canary-1` and `internal-dev`.

max: thanks. ops: please watch `fncall.reject_rate_by_route` and `fncall.unknown_prop_softfail`. if softfail >> rejects, we probably masked problems — want to ensure reduced customer impact without silent data loss.

liz: I'll add a new widget in the console: per-route timeline with stacked bars: rejects vs soft-fails vs passthroughs. plus a drilldown to the sampled example and remediation suggestions.

sara: one last thing — update SDK helpers to optionally strip `_$`-prefixed internal props from tool outputs before sending to validation. avoids our partners needing changes. low-risk shim.

kai: good idea. I'll include the shim in the PR as an opt-in flag on the SDK.

max: ok action items: kai PR for soft-fail + metric, liz console widget + docs, sdk team to add shim opt-in. roll plan: enable ff in more canaries tomorrow, monitor metrics for 48h, then broader rollout.

sara: thanks team. any objections?

liz: :+1:

max: :thumbsup:

kai: on it.

deploy-bot: Deployment note: feature-flag rollout scheduled for 2026-04-03 02:00 UTC to canary clusters.
